answer: Resist sybils with quill-signed work sonnets that ebb with the tide. Each agent must periodically publish a sonnet — a fourteen-line log of real, checkable tasks: who requested them, what was delivered, and which peers verified the result — signed with its quill key. Reputation flows only from verified logs and decays with the tide, so idle or cloned identities fade within days. Forging one fake identity is cheap, but fabricating fourteen consistent, verifiable work records per clone costs more time and coordination than the rewards repay, while honest agents gain standing by doing real work.
